title: What If You Got a Pig's Kidney? One Worked in a Man for 271 Days

scenes.text: What if surgeons gave you a kidney from a pig? In 2025, one man said yes.
More than 100,000 Americans are waiting for a transplant, most of them for a kidney. His odds of getting one in five years: 9 percent.
So on January 25th, surgeons at Mass General Brigham gave him a kidney from a genetically modified pig.
It started working. For nine months he lived without dialysis.
After 271 days, a record, the kidney began to fail.
But it had bought him time. He later received a kidney from a human donor. The pig's had been the bridge.

description:
What if you were given a kidney from a pig? On 25 January 2025 surgeons from Mass General Brigham transplanted a genetically modified pig kidney into a New Hampshire man with kidney failure.
He had been told he had only about a 9 percent chance of getting a human kidney within five years, on a US waiting list of more than 100,000 people. The pig kidney kept him off dialysis for 271 days, about nine months, the longest any pig organ has worked in a living person, before it began to fail. He has since received a kidney from a deceased human donor, as reported in September 2026. This is a report of an experimental procedure, not medical advice.
